consensus_summary: Primary consensus meaning is a place or season of trial, suffering, hardship, grief, spiritual darkness or low points (chiefly from Psalm 23:4), contrasted with mountaintops; common alternatives include divine judgment/decision, humility/lowliness to be exalted (Isa 40), restoration from desolation, and fertility/blessing.
book_summary: The low and humbled (opposite of the mountain-kingdom) that shall be exalted, per “every valley shall be exalted.”
consensus_core_identification: seasons/places of trial, suffering and spiritual low points
boundary_disagreement: Consensus primary covers any hardship, dark season or testing as a valley experience (plus secondary contextual uses); book centers the humble/status that is raised and treats the trial reading only as a noted common teaching, not the core symbol.
material_contradiction: Book replaces the consensus primary referent (trial/hardship) with a different referent (the lowly/humbled opposite mountain-kingdoms); the two cannot both serve as the core identification of the symbol in the same sense.
rationale: Blind responses settle on the Psalm 23 trial reading as primary (with high agreement that this is the settled popular/devotional consensus) and list the Isaiah 40 humility reading only as one common alternative. The book instead adopts the humility/exaltation identification as its entry while explicitly labeling the trial reading “commonly taught,” thereby replacing rather than narrowing or refining the central referent. Overlap on the single Isa 40 case does not preserve the consensus core.
strongest_objection: Dominant preaching, hymns and popular usage (acknowledged even in the book’s common-view note) treat valley via Psalm 23 as trials, so defining it as the humbled diverges from the primary settled association without nullifying that usage.
